newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Onsale sees Q2 sales advancing.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Onsale sees Q2 sales advancing.

text.p: Onsale Inc Chief Executive Officer Jerry Kaplan said he expects the Web auction company to report second quarter net sales growth that matches or exceeds analysts' 14-18 percent sequential rate forecasts.

"I think our growth was as the analysts expected, or better," Kaplan said in an interview ahead of the company's second quarter results, due on Tuesday. "I don't think there will be any surprises in that regard."
Kaplan said the number of registered bidders, which stood at 230,000 in early June, continues to rise steadily and there has been no material impact from new Internet shopping rivals.

Kaplan declined to discuss details of the results, citing the mandated "quiet period" ahead of earnings reports. Onsale has previously said it expects to operate at break even or a slight loss for the remainder of 1997 after showing a slight profit for five quarters through the first quarter of 1997.

The chief executive did say the company still plans to invest heavily over the next six months in building its brand and its operational structure to extend its early-mover advantage in the market for Internet shopping.
"Our goal is to become a kind of Costco for the Internet," he said of Onsale's online auction business model.

"We continue to see very healthy growth in the business as a result of the investments that we've made, primarily in establishing relations with suppliers, doing some significant brand building and stepping up customer acquisition efforts on the Internet directly," Kaplan said in an interview.

Onsale moved to five auctions a week from three a week on June 9, giving it about 66 percent more "shelf space" for selling goods, although Kaplan said actual volumes did not jump in proportion to the growth of available space.
Onsale shares closed Monday at 10, up 3/4 in light trade. Results are expected to be released Tuesday morning.

Citing a recent report by Montgomery Securities projecting that quarterly gross sales would rise by roughly 18 percent to $21.2 million in the second quarter, Kaplan said he "would not expect any downside" to such analyst estimates.

Kaplan said Onsale's sales continue to swing substantially towards a model where it is a principal, rather than an agent for its vendors. In the first quarter, net revenues were $12.3 million, but with agency sales it totaled $17.9 million.

Alex. Brown analyst Chris Fiess said he has a conservative estimate for net sales to have risen to $14 million in the second quarter, adding the company is continuing to expand the range of merchandise it is auctioning.

First Call estimates are for the company to post a net loss of $0.02 in the second quarter and a $0.03 a share loss for the full-year, with profits returning in 1998 when the First Call consensus estimate is for a $0.38 a share profit.
Kaplan said Onsale is still expecting to return to a more normal business model next year after making a heavy investment to build its business through the rest of 1997.

He said the company has increased its merchandise acquisition staff to 17 people from five and bought banner advertising space from Yahoo! Inc. both during the week it went to five auctions a week and subsequently.
When Onsale reduced its advertising presence for a period, Kaplan said Onsale's sales and margins had remained at the higher levels achieved during the advertising promotion.

Onsale, which provides for sales of excess goods through a public auction conducted over its Web site, had initially concentrated on personal computers and consumer electronics but is now expanding to sell other goods like Omaha Steaks.
Kaplan said the company is also working on other products and on a variety of brand promotion schemes.
"We are looking over the next six months to expand our presence on the major traffic sites through a variety of advertising and partnership arrangements," Kaplan said.

Kaplan noted the company faces competition from hundreds of Web sites, with some more established organizations such as Home Shopping Network parent HSN Inc recently launching online auction sites, but said that Onsale believes it has been establishing barriers to entry to competitors.
"The plain fact is that credible competition is emerging now. I don't want to seem glib, but the fact is we have not experienced any identifiable material impact at this point."
(-sam.perry@reuters.com, in Palo Alto, +1 415 846 5400)
